sections.title: Folding lehet or szabad into the verb itself
sections.content: Hungarian has a shorter way to say "may/can" than lehet + infinitive or szabad + infinitive: attach -hat or -het (vowel harmony, just like other suffixes you know) directly onto the verb, then add the same personal endings you already use in the present tense. Mehetek says almost the same thing as Lehet mennem — "I may/can go" — in a single word.

items.english: May I go? — Yes, you may.

items.spanish: Itt dohányozhatsz, de a kórházban nem.
items.english: You can smoke here, but not in the hospital.

sections.content: This is just a preview — a handful of common -hat/-het forms like mehet and dohányozhat, so you can recognize them. Several verbs change shape in front of -hat/-het (eszik → ehet, iszik → ihat); the full pattern, with all its stem changes, is coming in a later unit. For now, Mehetek and Lehet mennem are simply two ways to say the same thing.
